questions.question: A student makes a pinhole camera with two tiny pinholes placed very close to each other on the front face instead of one. What will they observe on the screen?
options: A single, twice-as-bright sharp image.
Two separate or overlapping dim, inverted images.
One upright image and one inverted image.
A single blurred image with no distinct features.

questions.question: In a pinhole camera, if the user widens the pinhole to three times its original diameter, how does this affect the image and why?
options: The image becomes sharper because more light is concentrated onto a single point on the screen.
The image becomes brighter but more blurred because more light passes through the hole in more directions, spreading onto the screen.
The image remains equally bright but becomes inverted because light rays cross over at a wider angle.
The image becomes dimmer and sharper because the larger aperture allows light to diffract more.

questions.question: An image of a candle is formed on a screen using a convex lens. If you cover the top half of the lens with an opaque piece of cardboard, what will happen to the image on the screen?
options: The top half of the candle's image will disappear.
The bottom half of the candle's image will disappear.
The entire image of the candle will remain visible, but it will be dimmer.
The image will become completely blurred and unrecognizable.

questions.question: How does a convex lens successfully form a sharp, clear image of a single point of a light source on a screen?
options: It filters out all light rays except those traveling parallel to the principal axis.
It redirects all the light rays originating from that single point so they are focused to the same point on the screen.
It reflects light rays off its front surface to form a virtual image that is projected forward.
It scatters light rays in all directions so that they evenly illuminate the screen.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how a converging lens refracts parallel light rays due to its shape?
options: It refracts (bends) light more at the edges than near to the centre.
It refracts (bends) light more near to the centre than at the edges.
It refracts all light rays by the exact same angle regardless of where they enter.
It only refracts light passing through the exact centre, while leaving edge rays completely straight.

questions.question: An object that is 1.5 meters tall stands 2.0 meters in front of a vertical plane mirror. Which of the following correctly describes the properties of its reflection?
options: It is 1.5 meters tall, inverted, and appears 2.0 meters behind the mirror.
It is 1.5 meters tall, upright, and appears 2.0 meters behind the mirror.
It is 3.0 meters tall, upright, and appears 1.0 meter behind the mirror.
It is 1.5 meters tall, upright, and appears on the surface of the mirror.

questions.question: A student stands facing a plane mirror wearing a T-shirt with the word 'PHYSICS' printed on it. How does the word appear in the reflection to the student, and why?
options: It appears upright and normal because plane mirrors do not alter text direction.
It appears upside down but in the correct left-to-right order because of vertical inversion.
It appears laterally inverted (flipped left-to-right) compared to the object when it is facing us.
It is completely illegible because the mirror scatters the letters in random directions.

questions.question: Why is the image formed by a plane mirror classified as a 'virtual' image?
options: The image can be projected onto a screen placed behind the mirror.
The image appears where light rays actually converge and intersect in real space.
The image appears where light rays seem to have come from, not where they actually come from.
The image is only visible in the dark and disappears under bright room lighting.

questions.question: A student observes a toy under a white light source. The toy reflects a large amount of red light, some green light, and almost no blue light. What colour does the toy appear to the student?
options: Blue, because the eye is highly sensitive to the absent light.
A shade of yellow or orange, determined by the relative amounts of red and green light it reflects.
Magenta, because red and blue lights are being combined by the eye.
Pure white, because white light is shining on it.

questions.question: A white screen is illuminated by a pure blue spotlight in a dark room. What colour does the screen appear to an observer, and why?
options: Black, because white screens can only reflect white light.
Blue, because white objects reflect all colours of light, so they look the same colour as the incident light.
Green, because blue light mixes with the yellow pigments in the white screen.
Red, because white objects reflect the complementary colour of the incident light.

questions.question: An object appears black when viewed under sunlight. What is happening to the light that hits this object?
options: All colours of light are reflected equally in all directions.
Only black light is being reflected, while red, green, and blue are transmitted.
All colours of light are absorbed by the object, and none are reflected.
The light is refracted through the object and focused behind it.

questions.question: A stage performer is wearing a pure red shirt. If the stage lighting changes to pure green light, what colour will the shirt appear to the audience, and why?
options: Red, because the shirt's pigments automatically emit red light when stimulated.
Green, because the shirt reflects the green light falling on it.
White, because red and green light mix on the shirt surface.
Black, because the red shirt does not reflect green light, so it is absorbed.

questions.question: A ray of light travels through the air and enters a flat, transparent glass block at an angle of 30 degrees to the normal. What happens to the direction of the ray as it enters the glass?
options: It continues in a straight line without changing direction.
It turns towards the normal, making the angle of refraction less than 30 degrees.
It turns away from the normal, making the angle of refraction greater than 30 degrees.
It reflects completely off the surface and does not enter the glass.

questions.question: When a ray of light exits a transparent plastic block and re-enters the air at an angle to the normal, how does its path change?
options: It bends towards the normal because air is less dense than plastic.
It bends away from the normal as it leaves the transparent material and re-enters air.
It stops refracting and travels parallel to the surface of the plastic block.
It reverses its direction completely and reflects back into the plastic.

questions.question: A laser beam enters a rectangular glass block with parallel sides at an angle, passes through the glass, and exits back into the air. Which statement correctly describes the path of the exiting beam compared to the entering beam?
options: It is bent at a 90-degree angle relative to the original beam.
It is in the exact same line as the original beam without any shift.
It ends up traveling in its original direction, but is displaced to the side.
It is focused to a single point outside the glass block.

questions.question: When looking at a coin at the bottom of a container filled with water, the coin appears to be closer to the surface than it actually is. What is the cause of this illusion?
options: Light rays are reflected off the bottom of the container, creating a real image above the water.
Refraction causes a virtual image to appear where the bent light rays seem to be coming from.
The water acts as a convex lens that magnifies the coin to make it look closer.
Total internal reflection prevents light from escaping, making the coin appear to float.

questions.question: A lighting technician mixes equal amounts of red and green light on a white screen. What secondary colour is produced, and what would happen if they then added an equal amount of blue light?
options: Yellow is produced; adding blue light makes the screen appear white.
Magenta is produced; adding blue light makes the screen appear cyan.
Cyan is produced; adding blue light makes the screen appear black.
Yellow is produced; adding blue light makes the screen appear green.

questions.question: A smartphone screen displays a bright yellow image of a banana. If you were to look at the screen through a powerful magnifying glass, what would you actually see?
options: Tiny yellow and white light-emitting pixels.
Tiny red and green lights (pixels) varying in brightness to make the yellow colour.
Tiny yellow filters moving in front of a white backlight.
A continuous, smooth yellow liquid that changes shape.

questions.question: A student directs a beam of white sunlight through a transparent triangular prism. What is observed on a screen placed on the other side of the prism?
options: A single, intensified spot of bright white light.
A visible light spectrum (rainbow) produced as the prism splits up the sunlight.
A shadow of the prism with no light passing through.
Three distinct spots of only red, green, and blue light with dark gaps between them.

questions.question: Two people look at the same coloured light. One person has a condition where their green-sensitive cone cells do not function. Why do they perceive the colour differently?
options: The light itself changes wavelength when entering their eyes.
Their rod cells are triggered instead of their cone cells, making everything look blue.
The colour we see depends on which cone cells are triggered to send a signal to the brain, and their inactive green cone cells change the triggered pattern.
Their brains are unable to process any electrical signals from the retina.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the structural components of a standard pinhole camera?
options: A closed box with a convex lens at the front and a mirror at the back.
An empty, closed box with a tiny hole on the front face and a screen on the back face.
A tube containing two plane mirrors angled at 45 degrees to each other.
An open box with a translucent screen in the middle and a small hole at each end.

questions.question: How do light rays from a candle flame travel to form an image on the screen at the back of a pinhole camera?
options: They bend at the pinhole to focus on a single point.
They travel in straight lines from the flame, passing through the pinhole to the screen.
They reflect off the inner walls of the camera before hitting the screen.
They spread out in curves to fill the entire back screen uniformly.

questions.question: A student pricks three separate, small holes close to each other on the front face of a pinhole camera instead of just one. What will they observe on the screen?
options: A single image that is three times brighter than before.
Three separate, dim, inverted images of the object.
A single, highly blurred image where three colors are separated.
No image at all, because the light rays cancel each other out.

questions.question: Why does widening the pinhole of a pinhole camera result in a brighter but much more blurred image?
options: The light rays are bent more strongly by the wider edges of the hole.
More light from each point on the object passes through the hole in more directions, overlapping on the screen.
The screen absorbs more light when the hole is larger, reducing contrast.
The wider hole acts like a diverging lens, spreading the light rays apart.

questions.question: If you cover the top half of a camera's convex lens with a piece of black paper, what will happen to the image formed on the screen?
options: Only the bottom half of the image will be visible on the screen.
Only the top half of the image will be visible on the screen.
The complete image will still be visible, but it will be dimmer.
The image will be inverted vertically but remain at the same brightness.

questions.question: What does a convex lens do to parallel light rays passing through it, and what is the term for the point where they meet?
options: It reflects them outwards; the point is called the virtual origin.
It refracts them so they travel more towards each other; the meeting point is the focus.
It refracts them away from each other; the point is called the dispersion point.
It absorbs them selectively; the point of maximum absorption is the dark spot.

questions.question: How does the refraction of light rays passing through the outer edges of a converging lens compare to those passing near its center?
options: Light is refracted more at the edges than near the center.
Light is refracted less at the edges than near the center.
Light is refracted by the same angle at both the edges and the center.
Light is only refracted at the exact center, while the edges reflect it.

questions.question: If you stand 1.5 meters in front of a flat, vertical plane mirror, how far behind the mirror does your virtual reflection appear to be, and how does its height compare to yours?
options: 3.0 meters behind the mirror, and half your actual height.
1.5 meters behind the mirror, and the same height as you.
1.5 meters behind the mirror, and twice your actual height.
0.75 meters behind the mirror, and the same height as you.

questions.question: You are wearing a t-shirt with the word 'PHYSICS' written on it and standing directly facing a plane mirror. How does the text appear in your reflection?
options: Upright but spelled backwards (laterally inverted).
Upside down but spelled from left to right.
Perfectly normal and readable, with no inversion.
Upside down and spelled backwards.

questions.question: Why is the image of an object in a plane mirror classified as a 'virtual image'?
options: The light rays physically converge at a point behind the glass of the mirror.
The light rays only appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror, where they do not actually come from.
The image can be projected directly onto a screen placed behind the mirror.
The image only exists when a camera is used to capture it.

questions.question: A stage prop looks yellow under white light because it reflects both red and green light. What color will this prop appear if it is illuminated only by pure green light?
options: Yellow
Red
Green
Black

questions.question: A performer wearing a white suit stands on a stage. If the stage lights are changed to pure blue, what color will the performer's suit appear to the audience, and why?
options: Black, because white objects absorb all colored light.
Blue, because white objects reflect all colors of light, including blue.
White, because the white fabric resists color changes under stage lighting.
Green, because blue light mixes with the yellow tones of the white fabric.

questions.question: Why does a black asphalt road feel much hotter on a sunny day compared to a white painted line on the same road?
options: The black road reflects all colors of light, which transfers energy to the surrounding air.
The black road absorbs all colors of light, converting the absorbed light energy into thermal energy.
The white paint absorbs more light than the black road, keeping the road cooler.
The black road transmits the light directly into the ground without absorbing it.

questions.question: A ray of light travels through the air and strikes the flat surface of a glass block at an angle to the normal. What happens to the light ray as it enters the glass?
options: It continues in a straight line without any change in direction.
It reflects entirely off the surface and does not enter the glass.
It changes direction as it enters the new medium, a process known as refraction.
It splits into a spectrum of colors instantly without changing its overall path.

questions.question: When a ray of light passes from air into a rectangular transparent plastic block at an angle, how does its path change relative to the normal line?
options: It bends away from the normal line.
It bends towards the normal line.
It stops and reflects back along the normal line.
It continues along its original path without bending.

questions.question: A laser beam enters a flat glass window pane at an angle, passes through, and exits back into the air on the other side. How does the exiting beam compare to the original entering beam?
options: It is traveling in a completely perpendicular direction to the original beam.
It travels in the original direction but is shifted to the side.
It is bent at a much sharper angle away from the original direction.
It is split into two beams that travel in opposite directions.

questions.question: When looking at a coin at the bottom of a container filled with water, the coin appears to be closer to the surface than it actually is. What is the reason for this illusion?
options: Light undergoes total internal reflection, creating a real image on the surface.
Refraction of light at the water-air boundary creates a virtual image where the light rays appear to come from.
The water acts as a plane mirror, reflecting an inverted image of the coin.
The light rays are absorbed by the water, making the coin look larger and closer.

questions.question: A lighting designer wants to create white light on a stage using only primary color spotlights. How can they achieve this?
options: By mixing equal amounts of red and green light.
By mixing equal amounts of red, green, and blue light.
By mixing blue and yellow light only.
By mixing unequal amounts of green and blue light.

questions.question: How does a modern display screen produce a yellow color in a specific region of an image?
options: By emitting light from dedicated yellow-colored micro-bulbs in that region.
By turning on its red and green sub-pixels at specific brightness levels while keeping blue off.
By filtering white backlight through a physical yellow dye embedded in the screen glass.
By rotating the blue pixels until they refract light at a yellow wavelength.

questions.question: If a person's green-sensitive cone cells are temporarily fatigued, and they look at a white screen that reflects red, green, and blue light, what color is their brain most likely to perceive?
options: White, because rod cells will compensate for the missing color.
Magenta, because mostly the red and blue cone cells will send signals to the brain.
Cyan, because green and blue signals will dominate.
Black, because all signals to the brain are blocked when one cell type is fatigued.
